headline: Majors hold above 200-day lines on $987M BTC ETF bid, but momentum diverges as shorts flush and whales rotate to cold storage.
paragraphs: Bitcoin is down 1.4 percent on the day, yet up 1.8 percent over the week and 21.2 percent over the month: a pattern that repeats across the entire major cohort. Six of seven tracked assets sit above their 200-day simple moving averages, Bitcoin among them. Ethereum, Solana, and BNB have completed golden crosses, suggesting trend confirmation in those names. But momentum tells a different story. RSI readings cluster between 58 and 67 across the board: a zone that looks constructive until you check MACD. Of the seven assets, only BNB and DOGE show MACD above its signal line. Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, XRP, and ADA all have MACD below signal, despite price sitting above the 200-day. That gap between trend (higher) and momentum (rolling over or flat) is the day's central technical tension. Price has climbed steadily from lows, but the accelerant is quieting.

Leverage positioning exposes a crowded upside. Bitcoin funding stands at 5.3 percent annualized, Ethereum at 9.3 percent: traders are paying to hold long exposure, and the market is expensive to short. Open interest in Bitcoin totals $2.18 billion, in Ethereum $1.53 billion. The long-short ratio on Bitcoin sits at 1.16 to 1, on Ethereum at 1.35 to 1. Neither is extreme, but Ethereum's tilt is meaningful. Liquidations in the last 3 to 4 hours show the real story: Ethereum has flushed $339 million in short positions versus $6.8 million in longs, a 50-to-1 skew. Bitcoin has seen $179 million in short liquidations to $130 million in long ones. That pattern, repeated across the tape, points to a crowded short being removed by price action rather than fresh buying. A squeeze in motion is not the same as a rally with conviction.

Whale flows and ETF inflows paint a bifurcated picture. Over the last 72 hours, $99.6 million net of Bitcoin has moved off exchanges, primarily from Coinbase Institutional (two outflows totaling $103 million) and balanced by smaller inflows to OKEx. Over the week ending September 7, $369 million of value moved off exchanges, the first week of outflow after three consecutive weeks of inflow totaling $1.75 billion onto exchanges. Stablecoin float sits at $310.6 billion, up just 1.45 percent on the month, a modest increase. Meanwhile, Bitcoin ETF net flows stand at $986.7 million inflow over the last five sessions (as of September 4), with three consecutive inflow days and $174.6 million on the latest session. Traditional finance is bidding steadily; large wallet holders are withdrawing coins to custody. The two moves need not contradict, but they suggest different time horizons: institutions accumulating via ETF, whales stashing coins, neither a sign of panic but neither a sign of capitulation either.

Sentiment sits at 71 on the Fear and Greed Index, labeled Greed, within a 30-day range of 27 to 74. That is elevated but not historically extreme. The crowd is comfortable, but a 47-point range in a month says volatility in mood has been sharp. Bitcoin dominance holds at 59.1 percent; total market cap is down 3.31 percent on the day yet Ethereum is down only 0.9 percent. Altcoins have outperformed on the day, a divergence that typically appears when rotation is in motion rather than when conviction is uniform. Solana, down 2.3 percent on the day, is up 35.7 percent on the month and still 58 percent below its 12-month high; XRP, down 1.8 percent on the day, is 55.3 percent below its 12-month peak. The phrase 'rally' applies to the month; the phrase 'rebound from depressed levels' may be more precise.

Watch three conditions to signal a shift. First, a loss of the 200-day by any major would reset the regime immediately; five of seven sit above it with conviction. Second, a funding flip on Bitcoin or Ethereum from positive to flat or negative would suggest that shorts are no longer being squeezed and longs are less willing to pay for duration. Today's 5.3 and 9.3 percent annualized rates are elevated enough that a snap downward is actionable. Third, a reversal in the whale outflow pattern or a stalling of ETF inflows would break the current equilibrium: institutions accumulating while large holders go cold would fail, and the two divergences would resolve into one conviction. The tape today is calm, elevated in mood, but fractured in its signals. Neither a reversal nor a breakout is evident yet; that divergence is the watch.
